todays_goal: Continue deliberate writing review: compare accurately, explain significance, and self-edit by finding and repairing a real weakness.

lessons.subject: writing
lessons.previous_learning: Day 20 writing improved factual content but still included awkward sentence structure and an unearned claim that no sentence sounded unclear.
lessons.course_context: Writing remains the daily review subject. The target is not just producing a paragraph but detecting and repairing weaknesses independently.
learning_objectives: Write a clear comparison using the same feature for both subjects.
Read writing aloud and identify a genuinely weak sentence.
Revise for accuracy, clarity, and completeness.
lessons.why_it_matters: Strong writers do not assume a first draft makes sense; they verify it and revise.

vocabulary.definition: reread your own writing and repair a real problem
a sentence that fully finishes the idea it starts
an explanation of how two things are alike and different

lessons.written_instruction: Atticus: after every sentence ask: Is it accurate? Is it clear? Is it complete? You do not earn a self-check point by saying everything is fine. You earn it by proving the writing is clear or repairing a real weakness.

worked_examples.title: Repair a crowded sentence
worked_examples.problem: The retina and camera sensor are similar can also make an image and different.
worked_examples.solution: The retina and a camera sensor are similar because both detect light. They are different because they handle the detected information in different ways.
worked_examples.explanation: The revision separates ideas and makes the comparison clear.

worked_examples.title: Finish why it matters
worked_examples.problem: This difference matters because a camera...
worked_examples.solution: This difference matters because a camera can record image data by itself, while human vision depends on the brain interpreting signals from the retina.
worked_examples.explanation: The explanation finishes the idea it starts.

worked_examples.title: Evidence to explanation
worked_examples.solution: This shows she values reliability more than finishing quickly.
worked_examples.explanation: The sentence explains what the action reveals.

guided_practice.prompt: Repair three awkward comparison sentences before drafting.

independent_practice.prompt: Write 7-8 sentences comparing Jalen and Mira. Include one similarity, two differences, evidence for both characters, and explain why one difference matters.
Complete the seven-step self-edit and rewrite your most awkward sentence.

exit_ticket.prompt: Score the paragraph using the strict 10-point mastery gate. Identify the real weakness you repaired.
exit_ticket.answer: Target 9/10 or better with a visible, meaningful revision.

lessons.voice_prompt: Be firm, concise, and specific. Have Atticus read sentences aloud. Ask only one check at a time: accurate, clear, or complete. If he says a sentence is fine when it is not, point to the exact confusing fragment but do not rewrite it for him. Use the whiteboard for a different sentence-repair example. Never dictate the assigned paragraph.
lessons.teacher_notes: Continue writing review until self-edit behavior is credible, not performative.
